candidates.phrase: most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth
candidates.rationale: The Confession directly attributes 'merciful' as an essential perfection of the one true God.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

candidates.phrase: to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy
candidates.rationale: Asserts mercy as one of God's attributes displayed in his providential governance of all things.
candidates.chunk_text: God the great Creator of all things doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will, to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy.

candidates.phrase: the manifestation of the glory of his mercy, in the eternal salvation of the elect
candidates.rationale: Affirms God's mercy as manifested in the salvation of the elect, a narrower but genuine instance of the predicate.
candidates.chunk_text: The end of God’s appointing this day is for the manifestation of the glory of his mercy, in the eternal salvation of the elect; and of his justice, in the damnation of the reprobate, who are wicked and disobedient. For then shall the righteous go into everlasting life, and receive that fullness of joy and refreshing, which shall come from the presence of the Lord; but the wicked who know not God, and obey not the gospel of Jesus Christ, shall be cast into eternal torments, and be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.

candidates.phrase: showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me
candidates.rationale: Directly asserts that the Lord God shows mercy, paralleling the Exodus 34:6 confession of divine mercy.
candidates.chunk_text: Which is the second commandment? A. The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

candidates.phrase: apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ
candidates.rationale: Asserts the reality of God's mercy toward the sinner as the ground of repentance.
candidates.chunk_text: What is repentance unto life? A. Repentance unto life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sin, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his sin, turn from it unto God, with full purpose of, and endeavor after, new obedience.

candidates.phrase: thankful acknowledgment of his mercies
candidates.rationale: Prayer is defined as including thankful acknowledgment of God's mercies, affirming God possesses mercy.
candidates.chunk_text: What is prayer? A. Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, for things agreeable to his will, in the name of Christ, with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.

candidates.phrase: most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates God as 'most merciful' among his essential attributes.
candidates.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

candidates.phrase: shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me
candidates.rationale: Quotes God's own first-person declaration of showing mercy, asserting mercy of God himself.
candidates.chunk_text: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it? A. The reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it, contained in these words, For I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments; are, besides God’s sovereignty over us, and propriety in us, his fervent zeal for his own worship, and his revengeful indignation against all false worship, as being a spiritual whoredom; accounting the breakers of this commandment such as hate him, and threatening to punish them unto divers generations; and esteeming the observers of it such as love him and keep his commandments, and promising mercy to them unto many generations.

candidate.phrase: the apprehension of God’s mercy in Christ to such as are penitent
candidate.rationale: Asserts God's mercy as a real attribute experienced by penitents, within the floor of affirming mercy of God.

candidates.chunk_text: GOD IS ONE. We believe and teach that God is one in essence or nature, subsisting in himself, all sufficient in himself, invisible, incorporeal, immense, eternal, Creator of all things both visible and invisible, the greatest good, living, quickening and preserving all things, omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true. Truly we detest many gods because it is expressly written: “The Lord your God is one Lord” (Deut. 6:4). “I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods before me” (Ex. 20:2–3). “I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me. Am I not the Lord, and there is no other God beside me? A righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me” (Isa. 45:, 21). “The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness” (Ex. 34:6).

candidates.locator: Article 20: The Justice and Mercy of God in Christ
candidates.phrase: God— who is perfectly merciful and also very just
candidates.rationale: Directly confesses God himself as perfectly merciful, asserting the predicate of the one God.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe that God— who is perfectly merciful and also very just— sent the Son to assume the nature in which the disobedience had been committed, in order to bear in it the punishment of sin by his most bitter passion and death. So God made known his justice toward his Son, who was charged with our sin, and he poured out his goodness and mercy on us, who are guilty and worthy of damnation, giving to us his Son to die, by a most perfect love, and raising him to life for our justification, in order that by him we might have immortality and eternal life.

candidates.phrase: God showed himself to be as he is: merciful and just
candidates.rationale: States God's own nature is merciful, a direct confessional assertion of the predicate of God.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe that— all Adam’s descendants having thus fallen into perdition and ruin by the sin of Adam— God showed himself to be as he is: merciful and just. God is merciful in withdrawing and saving from this perdition those who, in the eternal and unchangeable divine counsel, have been elected and chosen in Jesus Christ our Lord by his pure goodness, without any consideration of their works. God is just in leaving the others in their ruin and fall into which they plunged themselves.

candidates.phrase: God is merciful in withdrawing and saving from this perdition
candidates.rationale: Explicitly asserts God is merciful, specifying the mercy shown in election, within the floor of shared mercy.

survivors.locator: Chapter 2.1 — Of God, and of the Holy Trinity
survivors.phrase: most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth
survivors.rationale: The Confession directly attributes 'merciful' as an essential perfection of the one true God.
survivors.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

survivors.phrase: showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me
survivors.rationale: Directly asserts that the Lord God shows mercy, paralleling the Exodus 34:6 confession of divine mercy.
survivors.chunk_text: Which is the second commandment? A. The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

survivors.phrase: most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates God as 'most merciful' among his essential attributes.
survivors.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: kind and merciful, just and true
survivors.rationale: Confession directly asserts God is merciful as part of his essential nature.
survivors.chunk_text: GOD IS ONE. We believe and teach that God is one in essence or nature, subsisting in himself, all sufficient in himself, invisible, incorporeal, immense, eternal, Creator of all things both visible and invisible, the greatest good, living, quickening and preserving all things, omnipotent and supremely wise, kind and merciful, just and true. Truly we detest many gods because it is expressly written: “The Lord your God is one Lord” (Deut. 6:4). “I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods before me” (Ex. 20:2–3). “I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me. Am I not the Lord, and there is no other God beside me? A righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me” (Isa. 45:, 21). “The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness” (Ex. 34:6).

survivors.phrase: God is certainly merciful, but also just
survivors.rationale: The catechism directly asserts God's mercy as a divine attribute, affirmed alongside justice.
survivors.chunk_text: Q. But isn’t God also merciful? A. God is certainly merciful, but also just. God’s justice demands that sin, committed against his supreme majesty, be punished with the supreme penalty— eternal punishment of body and soul.

survivors.locator: Article 20: The Justice and Mercy of God in Christ
survivors.phrase: God— who is perfectly merciful and also very just
survivors.rationale: Directly confesses God himself as perfectly merciful, asserting the predicate of the one God.
survivors.chunk_text: We believe that God— who is perfectly merciful and also very just— sent the Son to assume the nature in which the disobedience had been committed, in order to bear in it the punishment of sin by his most bitter passion and death. So God made known his justice toward his Son, who was charged with our sin, and he poured out his goodness and mercy on us, who are guilty and worthy of damnation, giving to us his Son to die, by a most perfect love, and raising him to life for our justification, in order that by him we might have immortality and eternal life.

survivors.phrase: shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me
survivors.rationale: Quotes God's own first-person declaration of showing mercy, asserting mercy of God himself.
survivors.chunk_text: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it? A. The reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it, contained in these words, For I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments; are, besides God’s sovereignty over us, and propriety in us, his fervent zeal for his own worship, and his revengeful indignation against all false worship, as being a spiritual whoredom; accounting the breakers of this commandment such as hate him, and threatening to punish them unto divers generations; and esteeming the observers of it such as love him and keep his commandments, and promising mercy to them unto many generations.
